summary: Self-healing app for IT support that detects common IT issues and provides automated fixes or guided troubleshooting steps.

existing_features.title: Implement Internet Identity sign-in and use the authenticated principal as the user identity for all saved troubleshooting sessions and history.

Create a guided “Issue Intake” flow where a user selects an issue category (e.g., Network/Wi‑Fi, VPN, Email, Printer, Slow Computer, Account/Password, Software Install) and answers a short symptom questionnaire to generate a troubleshooting session.

Provide a built-in catalog of common IT issues with guided troubleshooting steps (“runbooks”), including decision points and clear instructions, and show the recommended runbook in the session detail view.

Support “automated fixes” as safe, simulated actions (since the app cannot directly control the user’s device), by presenting one-click actions that record an outcome and show what to do on the device (copyable commands or UI navigation) rather than executing system changes.

Add troubleshooting outcomes and escalation support: users can mark a session resolved, or escalate it by generating a concise incident summary (symptoms, steps attempted, results) that can be copied for an IT ticket.
Create a “History” view where users can search and filter their past sessions by status and category, and open a session to review the troubleshooting timeline.
Apply a coherent, distinctive visual theme for an IT support product and enforce it consistently across pages (typography, spacing, components, and tone), using English for all user-facing text.
Generate required static image assets and render them in the UI from frontend/public/assets/generated (do not fetch images through the backend).

new_feature_requests.summary: Build a self-healing IT support app that detects common IT issues and provides automated fixes or guided resolution steps.

Add backend support for troubleshooting sessions, including creating a session, updating its status (in_progress/resolved/escalated), appending step outcomes, and listing sessions for the current user.
Add user sign-in/account support (Internet Identity) so sessions and history are tied to the authenticated user.
